rich_summary: Bharata, learning that his mother Kaikeyi’s demands led to King Dasharatha’s death and Rama’s exile, erupts in fierce condemnation. He calls her cruel, accuses her of destroying the royal dynasty, and declares that the kingdom she secured for him has only brought him shame. Bharata insists Rama is beloved by all and vows loyalty to his elder brother rather than accepting the throne. To illustrate a mother’s grief, he recounts the story of the divine cow Kamadhenu, who wept on seeing two of her sons suffering under the plough, a scene even Indra witnesses with concern. The tale underscores the depth of maternal love and the cruelty of separating Rama from Kaushalya. Bharata ultimately vows to perform his father’s rites, restore Rama to Ayodhya, and live in the forest himself if necessary.

highlight_spans.why: Bharata’s opening outburst establishes the chapter’s emotional intensity and his furious rejection of Kaikeyi’s actions.
He declares that Kaikeyi’s deeds destroyed the dynasty and brought him shame rather than a rightful kingdom.
Introduction of the mythic example of Kamadhenu, shifting the speech into a symbolic lesson about maternal love.
The vivid image of Kamadhenu weeping for her suffering sons, witnessed by Indra, reinforces the universality of a mother’s grief.
Bharata’s vow: he will perform his father’s rites, restore Rama to the throne, and personally accept exile—revealing his devotion and moral stance.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bharata stands in the royal chamber of Ayodhya, pointing in fury at Queen Kaikeyi as courtiers watch in shock while he denounces her for Rama’s exile.
The divine cow Kamadhenu floats in the sky weeping radiant tears while Indra looks up in astonishment as her exhausted sons strain under a plough on the earth below.
Bharata solemnly vows before the court that he will bring Rama back to Ayodhya and take the forest life himself if necessary.
